<strategy>
The current approach uses a local optimization method, L-BFGS-B, starting from an initial guess. While this can be effective, it is prone to getting stuck in local optima. To improve the solution, we can leverage global optimization strategies and consider a more diverse set of initial constructions.

To enhance the search:
1. Use a different initial construction (like a periodic function or a more structured profile) to avoid local minima.
2. Employ a global optimization algorithm (like genetic algorithms, simulated annealing, or particle swarm optimization) to explore the solution space more thoroughly.
3. Consider a different discretization strategy (e.g., evenly spaced samples vs. adaptive sampling).
4. Use a more advanced mathematical formulation for the objective function, such as a convex relaxation or piecewise linear approximation.

Our approach will use a genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the function h. It is well-suited for this type of discrete optimization with constraints. We will start from the initial construction and also use additional structured profiles to ensure diversity in the search space.
</strategy>
